items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: Issue 1034 asks for an ordered, configurable route list for the GPT leg that falls through on pre-call unavailability and on runtime failure and records every attempt; implemented as gpt_leg.routes with attempts/fallback_reason, existing provider configs unchanged (tested).

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: Malformed routes (non-list, unknown names, repeats, empty) degrade to the legacy provider path; a route runner that raises becomes an error attempt and the chain continues; all-unavailable is a skipped leg listing every reason.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No new input surface beyond a config list validated against a closed set of three names; reasons are truncated to 300 chars; no shell, no new network target (same three existing legs).

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: 19 tests assert outcomes of the chain, the config resolver and a real main() run in which codex fails with a quota error and OpenRouter answers; the no-routes path is pinned to the old terminal-error behaviour.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: A failed route adds its own latency before the next route; worst case is the sum of the route budgets, which is the intended trade for an answer.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: New logic in lib/external_review_routes.py; tools/external_review.py grows by 13 lines (464 vs baseline 469); ruff clean.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: The leg result gains attempts and fallback_reason (additive); config gains an optional gpt_leg.routes list; check-external-review-keys reports codex_configured for a routes list that names codex.
